t: This is The Revells of Christendome, an engraving by Thomas Cockson. The image measures about 21.6 by 35.5 centimetres, and a copy is held in the Department of Prints and Drawings at the British Museum. Cockson, who lived from 1569 to 1640, was one of the earliest English engravers, and left a large number of portraits cut entirely with the graver in a neat, finished manner. His first and best-known work was made for John Harington's translation of Ariosto's Orlando Furioso.
